question: Identify an organelle found both in eukaryotic as well as prokaryotic.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Ribosomes**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Ribosomes** are the only organelles found in both eukaryotic and prokaryotic cells.
 
• They are responsible for protein synthesis in the cell.
 
• Ribosomes can be found floating freely within the cytoplasm or attached to the endoplasmic reticulum in eukaryotic cells.
 
• In prokaryotic cells, ribosomes are smaller (70S) compared to those in eukaryotic cells (80S).
 
• Despite the size difference, the fundamental function of ribosomes remains the same across both cell types.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Prokaryotic cells** do not have membrane-bound organelles, which distinguishes them from eukaryotic cells.
 
• **Eukaryotic cells** contain various membrane-bound organelles, including the nucleus, mitochondria, and lysosomes, which are absent in prokaryotic cells.
 
• The presence of ribosomes in both cell types highlights their essential role in the fundamental process of protein synthesis.
 
• The differences in ribosome size between prokaryotes and eukaryotes are due to variations in their ribosomal RNA and protein content.
